university_name: Quebec (Gouvernement du Québec -- education system / CEGEP)
requirement_text: College studies are one of the unique features of the Québec education system. Pre-university training bridges the gap between secondary and university studies. It leads to a Diploma of College Studies (DCS) and lasts two years. Technical training at the college level provides access to the job market or to university, so long as the university prerequisites are met; this training leads to a Diploma of College Studies (DCS) in a specific field and generally lasts three years.
source_authority_note: quebec.ca is the official Government of Quebec web domain; it is a .ca government domain but does not carry a .gov suffix, so it does not match the looksOfficial() predicate despite being unambiguously an official government source.
researcher_notes: This is the foundational structural fact behind the CEGEP-vs-non-CEGEP entry-point distinction: CEGEP (a 'college' level) sits between secondary school and university and is not optional for a Quebec secondary graduate entering the Quebec university system. Elsewhere on the same page: secondary education is a '5 year period (age 12 to 17)' beginning in Secondary I (grade 7), meaning a Quebec CEGEP-DEC holder has completed 5 years secondary + 2 years CEGEP = 7 post-elementary years before university, one more year than the 12-year (elementary+secondary only) pattern typical of other Canadian provinces and many other countries -- which is the structural root of why non-Quebec/international entrants are treated differently at the university admission stage (see McGill/Concordia/Bishop's records below).

university_name: Quebec (Gouvernement du Québec -- education system / CEGEP)
requirement_text: To be eligible for a Diploma of College Studies (DCS) program, an applicant must have: a Secondary School Diploma (SSD); or a Diploma of Vocational Studies (DVS) and have passed specific required Secondary V and Secondary IV courses; or meet alternative criteria the college deems equivalent. Applicants with six credits or less remaining before obtaining an SSD may still be eligible.
source_authority_note: quebec.ca is the official Government of Quebec web domain; it is a .ca government domain but does not carry a .gov suffix, so it does not match the looksOfficial() predicate despite being unambiguously an official government source.
researcher_notes: This is CEGEP-entry eligibility (secondary school -> CEGEP), distinct from the university-entry eligibility recorded separately for CEGEP graduates (CEGEP -> university).

university_name: Quebec (Gouvernement du Québec / Ministère de l'Immigration, de la Francisation et de l'Intégration)
requirement_text: To follow a course of more than six months in Québec as a foreign student, you must obtain the following two documents: Québec Acceptance Certificate (CAQ) for studies, issued by the government of Québec; Study permit, issued by the government of Canada. A 'more than six months' duration triggers the need for both authorizations; students pursuing programs of six months or shorter may be exempt from the CAQ requirement.
source_authority_note: quebec.ca is the official Government of Quebec web domain; it is a .ca government domain but does not carry a .gov suffix, so it does not match the looksOfficial() predicate despite being unambiguously an official government source.
researcher_notes: This is a Quebec-specific requirement layered on top of Canada's federal study permit, unique among the provinces researched in this pass, arising from Quebec's own immigration authority under the Canada-Quebec Accord. It applies uniformly to international students regardless of whether they enter via CEGEP or directly to university, so scope is 'Quebec (international)' rather than tied to the CEGEP/non-CEGEP axis.

requirement_text: You must have obtained, prior to the start of classes, a Diplôme d'études collégiales (DEC). Your application is reviewed on your overall R-Score (as determined by the Ministry) as well as a core R-Score average of any prerequisite courses (as calculated by McGill). Applicants must meet both the required global R-score and the required prerequisite average R-score in order to be offered admission. Students completing a Quebec Secondary V Diploma are not directly admissible to undergraduate study at McGill.
source_authority_note: mcgill.ca is the institution's own primary domain, not .edu/.ac./.gov.
researcher_notes: This record documents McGill University's own admission policy, used here as directly-verified evidence of how the general Quebec CEGEP/non-CEGEP structural distinction (see CA-0110) manifests at a real Quebec university. It is not asserted as a government-mandated rule uniform across all Quebec universities. Independent corroboration: Concordia University's own page (see CA-0117/0118) independently states the same 'Secondary V diploma holders are not directly admissible' rule and the same 'CEGEP DEC required' structure, which is why confidence is 'high' despite this being a single institution's policy.

requirement_text: Advanced Standing: students applying from certain school systems (CEGEP, IB, French Bac, AP, A-Level & AS exams, etc.), or from another university, may be eligible to receive up to 30 credits towards their McGill degree for university-level work already completed. Freshman/Foundation Year (U0): students coming from Canadian provinces outside the CEGEP system or from other countries may enter their undergraduate program at this level, and complete a 30-credit 'freshman year' before proceeding to take courses directed specifically towards their intended area of study. U1 Level (University Year 1): most CEGEP students will enter this level after completing a CEGEP 2-year DEC in Québec. Students entering McGill with 24 or more advanced-standing credits may also begin their studies as a U1 student.
source_authority_note: mcgill.ca is the institution's own primary domain, not .edu/.ac./.gov.
researcher_notes: This record documents McGill University's own admission policy, used here as directly-verified evidence of how the general Quebec CEGEP/non-CEGEP structural distinction (see CA-0110) manifests at a real Quebec university. It is not asserted as a government-mandated rule uniform across all Quebec universities. Independent corroboration: Concordia University's own page (see CA-0117/0118) independently states the same 'Secondary V diploma holders are not directly admissible' rule and the same 'CEGEP DEC required' structure, which is why confidence is 'high' despite this being a single institution's policy. THIS IS THE KEY RECORD FOR THE ASSIGNMENT'S CENTRAL QUESTION: it directly shows the structural entry-point difference in a real university's own terminology -- Quebec CEGEP-DEC holders normally enter at U1 (effectively a 3-year-to-degree path), while out-of-province Canadian and international students without CEGEP normally enter at U0 and complete an additional 30-credit Freshman/Foundation year before their specialized coursework begins (effectively a 4-year-to-degree path). This is not a 'penalty' -- it directly reflects that Quebec secondary school is structured as one year shorter than most other systems specifically because CEGEP supplies the difference (see CA-0110).
